findings.quote: Låntagaren fick säd och lämnade tillbaka lika mycket vid skörden, jämte ett tillägg på vanligen en åttondel.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, blind_pick C. Swedish sockenmagasin are documented as lending grain in kind against repayment in kind plus a fixed surcharge, one eighth being the figure usually cited; anyone who knows the institution leans C without the passage. Not a form leak: B (surcharge set annually by the sockenstämma) and D are substantive institutional variants a passage would have to settle, and A (repayment in money) existed elsewhere. Domain lean only -> flag.

findings.quote: Kyrkvärden förvarade båda nycklarna och kunde därför öppna magasinet utan att någon annan var närvarande.
findings.note: PARTIALLY, blind_pick null. Two options fall passage-blind on genre/institutional expectation: B inverts the two-lock/two-keyholder control that a magasinsordning exists to impose, and C ('behövde inte skrivas in förrän vid årets slut') inverts the bookkeeping such an ordinance prescribes. A (Mikaeli deadline, exclusion the following spring) and D (appointment rules) stay genuinely undecided without the text - materially better than chance, not decided -> flag.

findings.quote: Att han överdriver sparbankernas roll så till den grad att ingen enda av socknarna i boken stöder sambandet.
findings.note: PARTIALLY, blind_pick D. C is the absolutized twin of D ('ingen enda av socknarna') built on the same savings-bank critique; the moderate, evidence-specific member of such a pair is the usual key, which mildly signals D from form alone. A (kommunreformen 1863) and B (a single stämmoprotokoll) are substantive alternative criticisms the passage must settle, so one eliminable option only -> flag, not kill.

findings.quote: De ger läsaren en lättsam paus från bokens torrare partier, men har ingen bäring på recensentens omdöme.
findings.note: DECISIVE CHECK: the earlier stem-entailment kill is REPAIRED - the stem now only identifies the passages ('roligast att läsa') and asks an open 'vilken funktion' question; it neither restates nor entails any option, and no option is recoverable from the prompt. Residual PARTIALLY only, blind_pick B: A is disfavoured by the stem's own presupposition that the passages fill a function ('har ingen bäring'), and C answers a causal question about the wind-up rather than naming a function. B vs D still needs the passage -> flag, not kill.

findings.quote: Tuning is billed by the hour and always takes a larger share of the price than the metal.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, blind_pick D. Lathe tuning is broadly a fixed labour cost per bell while bronze cost scales with mass, so tuning outweighs the metal on a small bell and not on a heavy one - the trade-off D states is real founding economics and recognisable without the text. Form adds only a weak assist: A carries an absolute ('always') and C an over-broad 'far longer'. B remains a substantive claim about quoting practice that only the passage settles -> flag.

findings.quote: The bell has to leave the mould heavier, since the metal tuning removes must be there first.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, blind_pick A. Bells meant for close tuning are cast thicker because tuning is subtractive - metal can only be taken off on the lathe - which is standard campanology and decides A without the passage. D is additionally an absolute ('will always sound thinner') and C a non-sequitur (removing metal does not demand heavier fittings), but B is a substantive mechanism claim the passage must adjudicate -> flag, not kill.

findings.quote: He treats the disagreement as a matter of taste that measurement can never settle.
findings.note: PARTIALLY, blind_pick C. B is an eliminable absolute ('can never settle') and D is the dismissive extreme; that leaves the mild lean of A against the even-handed C, and attitude keys in expository features typically take the even-handed form - a test-wise lean, not a form leak. A and C rest on the same single trial, so the direction is genuinely undecided blind -> flag.

findings.quote: How a bell's partials are tuned, what that work costs, and how far founders take it.
findings.note: PARTIALLY, blind_pick D. Main-idea item: D is the three-clause synthesis that semantically subsumes A (what the work costs) plus the tuning material, while A is a single aspect, B a narrow counterclaim and C an evaluative thesis. Main-idea stems are inherently part-answerable by this shape and the corpus does not treat it as lethal (cf. elf-b11-001 q:5 pass), so flag rather than kill; the passage is still needed to rule out A's narrower framing.

findings.quote: Tre vintrars mätningar kan aldrig ge besked om hur ett ishus fungerade under en hel epok.
findings.note: PARTIALLY, blind_pick null. D is an eliminable absolute ('kan aldrig') and C sits off the stem's target - it objects to the reconstruction's fidelity as a copy rather than to the conclusion 'om isoleringen'. A (unrepresentative, tighter building) and B (confounded variable: packing rather than the sawdust layer) are both substantive objections to the insulation inference and the passage is required to say which one Karnstedt makes -> flag.

findings.quote: För att förklara varför handeln med sjöis till slut fick ge vika för de nya kylmaskinerna ute i staden.
findings.note: PARTIALLY, blind_pick D. Purpose-of-example stem: B jumps scope (one fishmonger's under-stair store bears on nothing about refrigeration displacing the trade) and C is the dismissive reading such examples rarely carry; that leaves A against D, with D the counterintuitive economic point examples of this kind usually exist to make - a test-wise lean, not a form leak. A stays substantive -> flag.

findings.quote: Den var den enda regel ishandeln följde, och samtliga firmor byggde sina ishus efter dess mått.
findings.note: PARTIALLY, blind_pick B. A is a double absolute ('enda regel', 'samtliga firmor') and falls to form alone. Beyond that the lean to B rests on a cross-question corroboration the orchestrator should see: within this stems sheet q:2 dates the corroborating trial to a modern reconstruction ('tre vintrars mätningar', a 1889 drawing rebuilt), which supports B's 'ett försök mer än hundra år senare' and undercuts D's early measurement series preceding the rule. Stems-internal, not passage knowledge; C stays substantive -> flag.

findings.quote: Tuning can cost more than the bronze on a small bell, and less than it on a heavy one.
findings.note: Domain economics gives a lean blind: tuning is largely fixed labour while bronze scales with mass, so D's small-bell/heavy-bell reversal is what a cost passage would say; C is its direct contradictory on the same axis and A carries a universal ('always takes a larger share'). But B (per-kilo quoting covering both operations) and C are substantive competing cost models, lengths and shapes are parallel, and nothing here is decidable from form alone - the passage is still needed to pick. World-knowledge answerability, not a structural leak.

findings.quote: Any bell tuned that closely will always sound thinner than one left as it came from the mould.
findings.note: Two options fall passage-blind: D overclaims with a universal ('Any bell ... will always'), and C is off-axis - heavier fittings and a stronger frame are hanging hardware, not a consequence of lathe work, which ordinary language reasoning shows without any bell knowledge. That leaves A vs B, and A is the only option framed as a consequence of *intending* tight tuning in advance, matching the stem's 'intends'. Materially better than chance but the A/B split is not decided without the text; the residual pull to A also needs the fact that tuning only removes metal, i.e. domain knowledge.

findings.quote: How a bell's partials are tuned, what that work costs, and how far founders take it.
findings.note: Umbrella tell, no domain knowledge required. For a 'mainly about' stem, D is the only option that names three coordinated subtopics, while A, B and C each assert a single-clause thesis; D also semantically contains A ('what that work costs' subsumes 'the price a parish pays'). A reader who knows nothing about bells picks the superset option from shape alone - the gate's 'one option semantically contains the others' mechanism. Note the repair DID land on the frame tell: How/Why is now balanced 2-2 (A/D How, B/C Why) and option lengths are level at 13-15 words, so the odd-one-out frame asymmetry is gone; the scope/umbrella asymmetry survived it. Fix by making D a single-thesis claim of the same grain as A-C, or by giving one distractor the same tripartite listing shape.

findings.quote: Luft tränger in, veden brinner upp i stället för att förkolna, och kolningen går förlorad.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, blind_pick B. The whole point of a charcoal kiln (mila) is oxygen-starved pyrolysis, so anyone who knows the craft knows an unnoticed gap in the covering lets air in and the wood burns to ash instead of charring. Domain knowledge, not form: A (slow cooling, half-charred wood) and C (charring dragging out past the six-to-nine-day span) are substantively plausible process outcomes to a reader without the craft knowledge, and only D is form-weak (the absolute 'ofelbart ... oavsett'), which eliminates one option, not three. No stem leakage, options are parallel in length and register -> domain lean only, flag.

findings.quote: Eftersom tjäran var ömtålig fick den bara framställas nära vattenvägar, medan kolet tålde långa landtransporter.
findings.note: PARTIALLY, no blind decision. A is eliminable without any domain knowledge because it contradicts the stem's own premise: the stem stipulates that tar could be produced FARTHER from the buyer than charcoal, while A asserts charcoal tolerated long land transport. C is weakly eliminable as it explains raw-material location rather than distance-to-buyer economics. That leaves B (charcoal bulky/many loads vs tar compact and high value per barrel) and D (charcoal crumbled at transhipment) as two substantively plausible economic explanations that the passage must settle - both are real historical facts about träkol and tjära, so neither can be picked blind. Two eliminations, better than chance, not decided -> flag.

findings.quote: Att kolräkenskaper aldrig kan säga något säkert om var ett hantverk faktiskt har bedrivits.
findings.note: PARTIALLY, lean A but not decided. Both scholars are invented, so no world knowledge applies; the eliminations are stem-fit and register. C overreaches with the absolute 'aldrig ... säkert', the standard shape of a filler objection, and D objects to the unit of measurement (vikt vs stig) rather than to the interpretation of the leveransgräns that the stem asks about. A and B both address the boundary itself and cannot be separated blind: which of them is the objection depends entirely on what Bostrand's interpretation was, which only the passage supplies. Not a structural leak - the four options are parallel in form and none restates the stem -> flag.

findings.quote: Att så gott som varje torparhushåll i häradet försörjde sig på både kolning och tjärbränning.
findings.note: PARTIALLY, lean C. Two options are weakly eliminable passage-blind: B overgeneralises from 'samma hushåll kunde' to 'så gott som varje torparhushåll i häradet', a scope error visible from the stem alone, and D smuggles in an unasked causal history (bruket's deductions for smulat kol) that no inference question of this shape would license. The remaining pair is genuinely contested: A (shared craft knowledge transfers) and C (seasonal complementarity of the work peaks) are both substantive inferences from the same premise, and only the passage decides which one it grounds. C being the more hedged formulation ('framför allt därför att') is a mild test-wise tell, but A is not phrased as an absolute either, so form alone does not separate them -> flag, not kill.
